title: test-0038-GEN-UPI
passage: Teacher: Today, let's clarify how UPI works. Remember, UPI is a public infrastructure, not a private company's app. When you use an app like PhonePe or Google Pay, they are just interfaces to access your bank account directly. Rahul: So, if I want to receive money, do I need to enter my UPI PIN? Teacher: No, Rahul. You only enter your PIN when you are sending money, never when receiving it. Priya: What about the safety of my details? A caller once asked me to install an app to 'fix' my account. Teacher: That is a dangerous scam. Never install apps or share OTPs, even if the caller claims to be from your bank. Bank employees will never ask for your PIN or OTP. Also, always check the name on the screen when scanning a QR code. If the name does not match the person you are paying, stop immediately. Finally, remember that UPI is a direct bank-to-bank transfer system; your money stays in your bank account, not inside the UPI app itself. If you delete the app, your money remains safe in your bank.
summary: Never install apps or share your OTPs, even if the caller says it's from your bank. Finally, remember that UPI is a direct bank-to-bank transfer system. Your money stays in your bank account, not inside the UPI app.
